s: Lightweight pub/sub broker designed for IoT: tiny packets, unreliable networks, and millions of low-power connections.
w: Clients connect over TCP/WebSocket with minimal handshake; topics use hierarchical paths (factory/sensor/temp). QoS levels (0-at most once, 1-at least once, 2-exactly once) trade reliability for overhead. Retained messages store last value per topic for late joiners. Last Will Testament messages notify others when a client disconnects unexpectedly. Session persistence survives reconnects.
use: IoT device telemetry ingestion from sensors and edge devices
Smart home automation (MQTT is the dominant protocol)
Vehicle fleet tracking with unreliable cellular connections
avoid: High-throughput data pipelines (Kafka is more efficient at scale)
Scenarios requiring complex message routing and filtering (broker-side rules limited)
pits: QoS 2 expensive at scale - use QoS 1 for most IoT telemetry; QoS 0 for fire-and-forget
Topic hierarchy explosion with uncontrolled device naming - enforce naming conventions
tips: MQTT is the HTTP of IoT - mention it as the default protocol for constrained devices
Last Will Testament is a unique and useful feature for detecting device failures
